commits.subject: feat(canary): FIX-1460 the GHA-dispatch canary reads its stems and their limits from job_registry — a slot (at/by) by its cron's period plus slack (169 / 25 h, three periods sub-hourly), a request-gated walker (stale_after: crs-summaries, bill-details) by its request (reaped missed, unconsumed 25 min, or a dispatch_log missed row in 24 h newer than its stamp), anything else unjudged; the hand list stays as the fallback for a registry read that fails (cc-324 Item 1)

[skip vercel] chore(fixes): sync after FIX-1460 — done.log records FIX-1460 local-only (93df1806, cc-324 Item 1) and cc-330's FIX-1459 prod-only (122afbba), which was on main unsynced

stopped_items: Read 4's STOP branch was taken (a branch, not a stop): the dispatcher re-arms a walker in the same tick that 3b reaps it `missed`, which replaces the key, so a daily read never sees D2's two key conditions while the route is dead and the row stays due. I added the prompt's fallback, the last 24 h of dispatch_log `missed` rows, as a third condition (stale when a miss is newer than the stem's last stamp). I kept D2's two key conditions alongside it rather than replacing them, because each can still be seen: a re-arm held back by a hold or an exclusion leaves `missed` on the key, and a dispatcher that stops ticking leaves the request unconsumed.

owed.what: the first sync-canary-check run on the new code (its 05:00Z slot): metadata.gha_dispatch lists every gha-dispatch registry stem on prod (bill-details once cc-330's row is there), crs-summaries judged by its request while it rests, gha_dispatch_stale and gha_dispatch_refused both tier null, no fallback line (metadata.gha_dispatch_source = registry)
